```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(data.table); library(knitr)
```

# Question and decision rule

Aim: run SNP-BLUP and ssGBLUP on the same 2 replicates of `r params$scenario`,
compare genetic response (NTM, NUE) and run time, and use the winner for all 20-replicate runs:
"higher response without demanding much larger run time".

**Rule (fixed before the runs; operational form of the aim):** ssGBLUP is used for all
runs only if **both**

1. its mean response over the 2 replicates is higher than SNP-BLUP for NTM **and** not lower for NUE, and
2. its mean evaluation time per generation is at most `r params$max_time_ratio` x that of SNP-BLUP.

Otherwise SNP-BLUP is kept (it is the current pipeline model, so a tie keeps the existing pipeline).

Response = change in the mean true breeding value of the cows from the first to the last generation
of genomic selection, in genetic SD units of the end of burn-in. NTM response = the NTM-weighted sum
of those changes (breed-specific NTM weights, file 00), so it measures progress in the current
breeding goal; NUE response = the change in NUE itself.

```{r read}
iw <- fread("params/index_weights.csv")[index == "GS_NTM"]
one <- function(dir, r, model) {
  tag <- paste0(params$scenario, "_", model, if (r > 0) paste0("_rep", r) else "")
  tr <- fread(file.path(dir, paste0("gs_trend_", tag, ".csv")))
  tm <- fread(file.path(dir, paste0("gs_eval_time_", tag, ".csv")))
  sd0 <- fread(file.path(dir, "gs_sdA0.csv"))
  g <- range(tr$generation)
  d <- dcast(tr[generation %in% g], breed + trait ~ generation, value.var = "mean_G")
  setnames(d, 3:4, c("g0", "g1"))
  d <- merge(d, sd0, by = "trait"); d[, dz := (g1 - g0) / sdA0]
  d <- merge(d, iw[, .(breed, trait, w = weight)], by = c("breed", "trait"))
  data.table(replicate = r, model = model,
             NTM = d[, sum(w * dz), by = breed][, mean(V1)],
             NUE = d[trait == "NUE", mean(dz)],
             eval_sec_per_gen = mean(tm$eval_sec))
}
# a run that did not finish (time limit or memory) leaves no files: it is reported and counts as "too slow"
one_safe <- function(dir, r, m) tryCatch(one(dir, r, m), error = function(e)
  data.table(replicate = r, model = m, NTM = NA_real_, NUE = NA_real_, eval_sec_per_gen = Inf))
res <- rbindlist(unlist(lapply(seq_along(params$sim_dirs), function(k)
  lapply(c("SNPBLUP", "ssGBLUP"), function(m) one_safe(params$sim_dirs[k], params$rep_ids[k], m))), recursive = FALSE))
# On the 7 GB machine the ssGBLUP runs were killed for exceeding memory (about 6.1 GB per
# process) in the first generation's evaluation, not for time; see logs/<step>.log and the README.
if (any(!is.finite(res$eval_sec_per_gen))) cat("Runs without output (did not finish within the step time or memory limit):",
  paste(res[!is.finite(eval_sec_per_gen), paste(model, "replicate", replicate)], collapse = "; "), "\n")
kable(res, digits = 3, caption = "Response over the selection period and evaluation time, per replicate")
```

# Decision

```{r decide}
m <- res[, .(NTM = mean(NTM, na.rm = TRUE), NUE = mean(NUE, na.rm = TRUE), eval_sec_per_gen = mean(eval_sec_per_gen)), by = model]
kable(m, digits = 3, caption = "Means over the 2 replicates")
s <- m[model == "SNPBLUP"]; g <- m[model == "ssGBLUP"]
ratio <- g$eval_sec_per_gen / s$eval_sec_per_gen
c1 <- isTRUE(g$NTM > s$NTM && g$NUE >= s$NUE)
c2 <- isTRUE(ratio <= params$max_time_ratio)
winner <- if (c1 && c2) "ssGBLUP" else "SNPBLUP"
writeLines(winner, "params/eval_model_choice.txt")
fwrite(cbind(m, time_ratio_vs_SNPBLUP = c(1, ratio)[match(m$model, c("SNPBLUP", "ssGBLUP"))]),
       "params/eval_model_test.csv")
```

* Higher response (NTM higher and NUE not lower): **`r c1`**
* Evaluation time ratio ssGBLUP / SNP-BLUP: **`r round(ratio, 2)`** (limit `r params$max_time_ratio`): **`r c2`**
* **Model used for all replicate runs: `r winner`** (written to `params/eval_model_choice.txt`).

With only 2 replicates the response difference is not tested statistically; the rule above is a
practical choice, by design, not a significance test.
